title: Course Schedule
kidExplanation: Classes with prerequisites. Can you finish them all without a loop of 'must take A before B before A'?
plainProblem: Course Schedule: Classes with prerequisites. Worked example — input: numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[1,0]]; expected output: true. Why: Possible. Interview pattern to name out loud: Graph BFS / DFS.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Course Schedule”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[1,0]] should still produce true.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: The problem can be reduced to detecting cycles in a directed graph. We can represent the course prerequisites as directed edges between nodes (courses). If there is a cycle in the graph, it means we can't complete all courses.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
